_comment: Every leaf setting is {value, default, description} so an admin can see current vs. default and what a key does without opening SETTINGS.md. 'value' is the only field the provider actually reads; 'default' and 'description' are informational, written once when the file is (re)seeded and otherwise ignored by the parser.

data_directory.description: Where the log, clone-state file, and this settings file itself live. Defaults to the script's own folder.

log_file.description: Log filename, relative to data_directory unless given as an absolute path.

clone_state_file.description: Persisted in-flight-clone tracking, relative to data_directory unless absolute. Survives a provider restart.

settings_reload_interval_seconds.description: How often this file's own last-write time is checked and reloaded if changed. Checked opportunistically on incoming requests, no background timer.

capabilities._comment: Mirrors RAS CPF's provider/initialize response field-for-field -- what this file's admin sets here is exactly what RAS is told the provider supports.

guests_polling_rate.description: Seconds between RAS's own guests/get polls per guest, as advertised to RAS (RAS decides whether to honor it).

tasks_polling_rate.description: Seconds between RAS's tasks/get polls for an in-flight task. Must stay above cloning.pipelined_cloning.completion_seconds, or a clone that meets that threshold still waits for RAS's next scheduled poll.

tasks_polling_retries.description: How many tasks/get polls RAS makes before giving up on a task, as advertised to RAS.

template_method.description: CPF template-creation contract level: "none", "basic", or "versioning". "basic" is required for linked clones (can_link_clones).

can_link_clones.description: Master switch for linked clones -- advertised to RAS AND what Handle-GuestClone actually gates on (single source of truth, deliberately not split across two settings). Off by default: confirm the storage backend supports it first (see DISTRIBUTED-PLACEMENT.md / LINKED-CLONES.md #3) before enabling on a new cluster.

linked_clone_fallback.description: What happens when RAS asks for a linked clone but the live source is not a Proxmox template. "full": log and proceed as a full clone. "error": refuse instead.

pipelined_cloning._comment: Lets RAS submit the next guests/clone before a full clone's disk copy actually finishes. See PIPELINED-CLONING.md. Has no effect on linked clones (their real completion is already sub-second).

enabled.description: Master switch. false = a clone task only reports 'completed' once Proxmox's own job finished (full clones only -- linked clones are unaffected either way).

completion_seconds.description: Seconds after clone submission before a still-running full clone is reported 'completed' anyway. Keep at or below (capabilities.tasks_polling_rate - 1).

max_concurrent_clone_operations.description: Even past completion_seconds, a clone only pipelines through if fewer than this many full clones are currently active -- the real concurrency gate on Proxmox's disk-I/O-heavy clone jobs.

start_poll_interval_seconds.description: How often guests/control(start)'s defensive guard polls the real Proxmox clone task while waiting for it to finish, before ever calling Proxmox's own start endpoint.

start_max_wait_seconds.description: Ceiling for the same wait -- fails loudly rather than hanging the shared stdin/stdout pipe on a stuck clone.

timeouts._comment: Deletion, caching, retry, and sweep timing -- everything that bounds a wait or a retention window but isn't specific to pipelining or load balancing.

delete_hard_stop_poll_interval_seconds.description: Poll interval for the forced hard stop guests/control(delete) issues before destroying a VM.

delete_hard_stop_max_wait_seconds.description: Ceiling for the same wait -- fails loudly rather than hanging if a hard stop never completes.

cluster_resources_cache_ttl_seconds.description: How long the bulk VM listing (GET /cluster/resources?type=vm) is reused before re-fetching. Keep in sync with capabilities.guests_polling_rate.

recently_deleted_retention_seconds.description: How long a VM this provider deleted stays hidden from guests/list even if Proxmox's own view hasn't caught up. Self-expiring, so a reused VMID is never permanently hidden. Also the window cloning.load_balancing.preserve_node_on_recreation checks.

recently_controlled_retention_seconds.description: After this provider issues a control action, how long power state is read live (authoritative) instead of from the lagging cluster listing.

recently_stopped_retention_seconds.description: After this provider's own 'stop', how long the guest-agent probe is skipped outright instead of racing Proxmox's teardown.

template_delete_confirm_seconds.description: After guests/convert(is_template:false), how long to wait for a guests/control(start) before concluding RAS deleted the Template (not entering maintenance) and removing the rasTemplate<id> tag.

recently_converted_retention_seconds.description: Same idea as recently_controlled, for the template flag after a guests/convert.

sweep_min_interval_seconds.description: The opportunistic re-check of every OTHER in-flight clone on each guests/get is throttled to at most once per tracked id per this many seconds.

completed_clone_task_output_retention_se.description: How long a completed clone task's clone_id is remembered after tracking is cleared, so a racing tasks/get can still answer correctly.

control_retry_max_attempts.description: guests/control retries this many times total on a transient Proxmox 5xx. Set to 1 to disable retrying.

tag_write_timeout_seconds.description: Timeout on every rasTemplate/rasClone tag PUT -- best-effort metadata that must never dominate the request it rides along on.

http_timeout_seconds.description: Default timeout (seconds) for a Proxmox API call that does not set its own tighter timeout. One retry on a fresh connection happens automatically before a failure is returned.

clone_tracking_max_age_seconds.description: Hard ceiling (seconds) a clone stays tracked without reaching ready before its tracking is force-retired regardless of state -- the backstop for a clone deleted outside guests/control(delete), or one that never becomes ready for any other reason.

load_balancing._comment: Spreading clone compute across cluster nodes instead of always landing on the source template's own node. See DISTRIBUTED-PLACEMENT.md. Requires shared storage (e.g. Ceph/RBD) -- target only moves compute, never disk.

enabled.description: Master switch. false = every clone lands on the source's own node, exactly like before this feature existed. A live scheduling change on real infrastructure -- opt in deliberately.

strategy.description: "resource": pick the least-loaded eligible node per resource_metric. "round_robin": ignore load, cycle eligible nodes in name order.

resource_metric.description: Only used when strategy = "resource". "cpu", "ram", or "both" (average of the two load fractions). Lower is better in every case.

excluded_nodes.description: Node names never chosen as a clone target even if online, e.g. a node that also runs the RAS Connection Broker/this provider. Case-sensitive, must match Proxmox's node names exactly.

node_stats_cache_ttl_seconds.description: How long a fetched node-resource snapshot (GET /cluster/resources?type=node) is reused. Separate from timeouts.cluster_resources_cache_ttl_seconds -- different endpoint, different freshness need.

preserve_node_on_recreation.description: When RAS deletes a guest and clones a new VM under the same name, land it back on the node it was already on instead of re-running strategy selection. Only applies within timeouts.recently_deleted_retention_seconds of the delete.

enabled.description: When RAS deletes a guest and clones a new VM under the same name, give its NIC(s) the same MAC address(es) the old one had -- keeps a DHCP reservation or MAC-keyed licensing continuous across a recreate. Off by default.

timeout_seconds.description: Explicit timeout on the guest-agent network-interfaces call. A healthy agent answers in tens of ms; Proxmox's own default would otherwise block ~3s per agent-less VM.

quarantine_after_seconds.description: How long a VM must be confirmed agent-less before it's tagged rasQuarantine and the agent stops being probed (paired with quarantine_min_failures below).

quarantine_min_failures.description: How many separate poll failures, alongside quarantine_after_seconds, before quarantine tagging kicks in.

enabled.description: Periodically flags (log + rasOrphanCandidate tag only, never stops or deletes) a rasClone-tagged VM this provider is no longer tracking AND RAS hasn't polled recently -- a lead that RAS may have permanently lost track of the guest.

check_interval_seconds.description: How often the audit runs, throttled opportunistically like everything else in this provider (no background timer).

stale_poll_after_seconds.description: How long since RAS's last guests/get for a VM before it qualifies as a candidate.

tags._comment: Proxmox tag names this provider reads/writes -- a single ';'-separated string on the VM's own config, visible and editable by an admin in the Proxmox UI too.

ras_exclude_tag.description: Manual, admin-set -- this VM does not exist for RAS at all (never listed, guests/get reports not-found).

ras_template_tag_prefix.description: Automatic -- <prefix><id> applied to a clone's SOURCE, where <id> is the source's own VMID.

ras_clone_tag_prefix.description: Automatic -- <prefix><id> applied to a fresh clone once its Proxmox job is confirmed done, where <id> is the SOURCE's VMID.

pool_name.description: Proxmox pool id (poolid) this provider is scoped to. Empty (default) = no pool filtering, every pool and every unpooled VM is visible. When set, a VM not in this exact pool is invisible to RAS -- never listed, guests/get reports not-found -- identically to ras_exclude_tag. Case-sensitive, must match the poolid exactly.

inherit_on_clone.description: Whether a clone is created in its source template's own Proxmox pool (via the clone API's own 'pool' parameter), so pool-scoped visibility and any pool-based Proxmox permissions extend to clones automatically. Independent of pool_name -- applies whenever the source VM actually belongs to a pool, even if pool_name filtering itself is off.

log_level.description: 3 = Standard (lifecycle + errors only), 4 = Extended (+ every lifecycle/control/tag event), 5 = Verbose (+ every RPC and HTTP call). Accepts the number or the word.

log_rotate_max_mb.description: Log file size (MB) that triggers rotation.

log_rotate_max_generations.description: How many rotated generations are kept.
